title: Jet-lagged work trip
hero: frosted-glass bedside clock
start: A compact hotel-room writing desk of brushed graphite metal fills the midground of a pale neutral tabletop, about the length of a forearm, with a chamfered top and two slim legs. At its centre sits a closed graphite laptop, its lid seams crisp. On the left stands a squat bedside clock the size of a matchbox, its sandblasted frosted-glass front a plain dial with tick marks, lit softly from within. Its single acid-lime hour pointer points to the dead middle of the night. To the right lies an ivory card key sleeve, folded once, beside an unopened ivory envelope with a crisp flap. Behind the desk a tall frosted-glass window panel glows with faint blurred city dots. Fine dust rests on the desk edge, and the room is still, tidy and wide awake.
end: The same desk, now crowded. The bedside clock has multiplied into more than a dozen frosted-glass clocks of shrinking sizes, spilling from the left edge across the laptop and toward the right, each dial showing its pointers at a different angle. The original clock tips back on its rear edge, its acid-lime hour pointer still pointing to the dead of night while the copies around it show other hours. The laptop lid has been pushed half open and a small clock is wedged in the hinge. The ivory envelope is caught mid-slide off the right edge, flap torn, and the card key sleeve flutters in the air. Behind, the window's city dots have smeared into long horizontal streaks across the frosted glass. A haze of fine dust hangs over the pile, drifting away from the original clock.
apocalypse: A wide miniature plain of cracked frosted-glass slabs stretches under a dim, even dusk toward a low horizon of blurred glass towers. In the foreground, a building-sized graphite desk lies tilted and half sunk, one leg snapped, its surface crusted with dust. Scattered across the plain are hundreds of weathered clock dials, bleached and cracked, half buried like dropped coins, their pointers frozen at every angle. The giant laptop lid juts up behind the desk like a split wall. In the middle distance, a slim graphite tripod crane with a lime-painted jib lowers one clean frosted dial onto a low graphite plinth beside the desk, its pointers already set to a single chosen hour. A thin graphite rail runs from the plinth toward the towers, carrying a second small clock outward to match it.

title: Corporate gym
hero: graphite office treadmill
start: On a pale neutral tabletop, a small office desk of brushed graphite metal sits at left, about the size of a shoebox, with an ivory paper blotter, a frosted acrylic desk lamp and a neat stack of three ivory folders. A slim graphite desk chair stands beside it with a folded ivory jacket over its back. Close on the right, about a pencil's length, stands a miniature treadmill: graphite side rails, a chamfered handlebar and a belt of finely ribbed ivory card. Its acid-lime start button, a single round cap on the console, is the only colour in the frame. A frosted acrylic water bottle stands at its foot. The treadmill is switched off and the belt sits still. Faint scuffs mark the belt's centre, and fine dust coats the desk corner nearest the machine.
end: The same desk and treadmill, now in motion. The acid-lime start button is pressed flat and the belt runs fast, and the graphite desk has been dragged half onto it, legs skidding backward and scoring pale lines in the tabletop. The three ivory folders slide off the blotter in a fanned arc toward the rear. The desk chair has rolled off the back of the belt onto a narrow graphite rowing rail and is caught mid-glide, the ivory jacket lifting off its backrest. The frosted lamp leans at a steep angle, its glow swinging across the belt. The water bottle is tipped, a fine spray of acrylic beads flying from its neck. Ribbed card dust from the belt hangs in the air, streaming away from the console.
apocalypse: A flat, cracked salt pan of pale ivory card stretches to a hazy horizon under low side light. Across it lie the ruins of a giant gym floor: a treadmill the size of a warehouse, its belt torn and draped across the ground like a dropped ribbon, its graphite rails bleached and bent. Nearby a rowing rail runs straight out into the distance, half buried, with a chair base seized onto it. Colossal ivory folders lie flattened into the crust. The frosted lamp stands snapped in two, its head filled with dust. In the midground, a low graphite gantry on four thin legs straddles one plain graphite desk, its lime lifting clamps setting the desk down squarely on firm, still ground beside the belt, legs level for the first time in years.

title: Teleprompter runaway
hero: graphite teleprompter with paper script rollers
start: A studio teleprompter about the height of a wine bottle stands in the centre of a pale neutral tabletop. Its hood is matte graphite metal with chamfered edges, and an angled pane of sandblasted frosted glass sits at the front, showing a few soft, blank grey bars. Beneath it, a long ribbon of ivory paper script winds between two graphite rollers, and a small acid-lime speed knob on the side housing is set to its lowest notch. To the left, an empty graphite stool with a folded ivory jacket over its seat is turned toward the glass. To the right, a short stack of spare ivory script rolls rests on a graphite tray. Fibres of the paper ribbon catch the light, and a faint dust line marks where the ribbon rubs the housing.
end: The same prompter, now running away. The acid-lime speed knob is twisted hard to its stop, and the graphite rollers spin so fast that the ivory script ribbon whips out of the housing in long looping arcs. The ribbon pours across the tabletop toward the left, coiling around the stool legs and dragging the folded jacket half off the seat. The spare rolls on the right have unwound in sympathy, their tails lashing off the tray. On the frosted glass the blank grey bars have smeared into a single streak. One roller has jumped its bracket and hangs tilted. Torn scraps of paper hang in the air, and fine paper dust drifts from the rollers, every loop traceable back to the housing.
apocalypse: A deep canyon walled with compacted layers of ivory script paper runs away from the viewer toward a pale gap of sky. The strata are creased, torn and yellowed at their edges, like sediment laid down over years. On the canyon floor lies the enormous graphite hood of the prompter, tipped on its side, its frosted glass cracked into a milky web. One roller the size of a water tank protrudes from the wall, its ribbon still fused into the rock. The stool's legs stick up from a drift of scraps. In the midground, a slim graphite winding rig on a short rail carries a lime take-up spool, reeling one clean length of paper ribbon at a slow, even pace from the canyon floor onto a fresh graphite roller.

title: Concession overflow
hero: frosted-glass popcorn cabinet with kettle
start: A cinema concession counter of brushed graphite metal runs across the midground of a pale neutral tabletop, about a forearm long, with a chamfered front edge. On its left end stands a popcorn cabinet the size of a shoebox: sandblasted frosted-glass walls, a graphite roof and a small graphite kettle hung inside. The kettle's acid-lime lid tips gently open, releasing the first few puffs. A shallow layer of popcorn made from crumpled ivory paper nuggets covers the cabinet floor. On the right sit three empty ivory card cartons, crisply folded and unmarked, and a graphite scoop hangs on a hook. A folded ivory apron rests on the counter, left behind at the end of a shift. Paper crumbs dot the counter, and a faint haze clings to the frosted glass.
end: The same counter under an overflowing kettle. Its acid-lime lid is flipped fully back and ivory paper popcorn erupts in a thick column, packing the frosted cabinet solid and bursting its front door open. Popcorn cascades along the counter in a drift that has swallowed the three cartons, tipping one onto its side. The graphite scoop has been knocked off its hook and is caught mid-fall off the front edge, trailing kernels. The folded apron is being carried toward the right end on a rolling wave of puffs. Loose pieces hang in the air above the kettle, a pale dust rises from the drift, and every ripple in the pile slopes back to the cabinet on the left.
apocalypse: A wide field of pale ivory popcorn dunes, crumpled paper puffs weathered grey at their crests, rolls away to a low horizon. Half buried in the nearest dune is a giant graphite counter, its front edge snapped and its surface cracked. Behind it the frosted cabinet has collapsed into shards the size of doors, their milky edges poking from the drifts, and the kettle lies on its side like a toppled bell. A graphite scoop the size of a boat is wedged upright in the middle distance. Across the foreground, a slim graphite plough rig on narrow caterpillar tracks pushes its lime blade forward, carving one clean, level path through the dunes back toward the counter, the cleared floor behind it smooth, pale and swept.

title: Billable hours
hero: graphite punch clock and ivory time cards
start: A heavy lawyer's desk of matte graphite metal, about the size of a shoebox, sits squarely on a pale neutral tabletop, its top chamfered and polished by use. A single ivory time card lies at its centre, crisp and lined with blank ruled rows. On the left, a graphite punch clock the height of a mug stands on a graphite plinth, a plain dial with tick marks behind sandblasted frosted glass, its acid-lime punch lever raised and ready. On the right, a frosted acrylic desk lamp glows over a closed ivory case file bound with a paper band. A graphite chair is pushed in, a folded jacket over its back. Pinprick punch holes mark the card's first row, and fine dust sits in the desk's seams.
end: The same desk sinking under paper. The acid-lime punch lever is jammed down, and the punch clock spits ivory time cards in a continuous stream from its slot, each card flicking into the air before it lands. Cards have stacked into teetering columns across the desktop, burying the case file and pressing the lamp over at an angle. Under the weight, the desk's four legs have punched through the tabletop, and it has sunk to its drawers in a cracked crater, fracture lines radiating outward. The chair has rolled backward and tipped, its jacket sliding off. A fan of cards hangs mid-flight off the right edge. Paper dust and tiny punched circles drift in the air, all rising from the clock.
apocalypse: A vast basin of layered ivory time cards, packed into sediment and weathered into ridges, spreads toward a hazy horizon. At its centre, a giant graphite desk sits deep in a sinkhole, only its chamfered top and one drawer front showing, cracked and bleached. The punch clock lies toppled beside it, its frosted front shattered and its slot choked with fused cards. The lamp's frosted shade juts from a ridge like a broken dome. Countless punched paper circles lie scattered like gravel. In the midground, a slim graphite drilling tower on three splayed legs lowers a lime core tube into the sinkhole beside the desk, drawing out a single clean ivory card and setting it into a fresh, upright punch clock on a small graphite platform.

title: Cloned yourself
hero: graphite desk with small photocopier
start: One tidy workstation sits on a pale neutral tabletop: a graphite desk the size of a shoebox with crisp chamfered edges, a graphite chair tucked squarely under it, and a single frosted acrylic mug with a faint ring of dried coffee inside. At the desk's right corner sits a small graphite photocopier the size of a matchbox, its sandblasted frosted-glass bed lit from beneath. Its acid-lime copy button glows, pressed once. A neat ivory notepad lies squared beside the mug, and a folded ivory cardigan hangs over the chair back. The desk's machined surface shows fine concentric marks, and light dust sits in the copier's seams. Everything is single, straight and freshly set, one of each.
end: The same desk, copied again and again. From the original in the foreground, a row of desks marches off to the right, each a slightly worse copy: the second soft at its edges, the third warped and pale, the fourth made of crumpled ivory card, the last a flimsy folded sheet collapsing under its own mug. The acid-lime copy button on the original copier is stuck down, and a fresh desk is sliding out of its side. Mugs tip and spill thin grey streaks, chairs lean further with each copy, and cardigans fray into loose fibres. A drift of misprinted ivory sheets flies up between the copies, all tracing back to the copier at the head of the line.
apocalypse: A long, flat plain stretches to a vanishing point, lined with a receding avenue of ruined desks, each more eroded than the last until the far ones are only mounds of grey paper pulp. Near the viewer, the original graphite desk stands the size of a house, weathered and scuffed but whole, its copier toppled on the ground beside it with the frosted bed cracked. Bleached mugs lie scattered like boulders, and fallen chairs splay across the plain. Drifts of misprinted sheets fill the gaps. In the midground, a slim graphite crane on a single track lowers a lime rectangular frame over the original desk, fixing it in place, while a small graphite sweeper beside it begins pushing the nearest copies into neat bales.

title: Undercoat upsell
hero: graphite sedan on a sales-desk turntable
start: A small car-lot sales desk of brushed graphite metal sits at left on a pale neutral tabletop, with a frosted acrylic desk lamp and a graphite pen holder. On the desk lies one ivory add-on form, a single crisp sheet with blank boxes. To the right, a model sedan the size of a loaf of bread stands on a graphite turntable, its body matte graphite and its windows sandblasted frosted glass. A small acid-lime price tag hangs on a string from its mirror, blank on both fronts. Along the back edge lies a thin drift of ivory paper flakes like light snow. A cold frosted mug sits by the lamp. Tyre scuffs mark the turntable, and fine flakes rest on the sedan's roof.
end: The same desk and sedan, buried in add-ons. Ivory forms stack on the desk in tall slanting towers, then spill across the gap and pile onto the car: sheets pinned under its wipers, wedged in its door seams, heaped on its roof and bonnet. The weight has pressed the sedan's suspension flat and tilted the turntable, lifting one wheel into the air. The acid-lime price tag swings sideways on its string, pinned against the frosted window by a sliding sheet. The desk lamp is knocked over, its glow pooling on a drift of forms. Loose sheets hang mid-fall from the roof toward the right, and flakes swirl up off the back edge, all spreading outward from the desk's first stack.
apocalypse: A wide, windswept plain of ivory paper snow stretches to a pale horizon, broken by low ridges of compacted forms. Rows of giant graphite car bodies sit half buried in the drifts, frosted windows cracked and packed with sheets, roofs sagging under old paper crusts. Toward the left, the sales desk rises like a tilted slab from a mound of forms, its lamp snapped off. In the midground, one sedan has been dug out: a slim graphite gantry on two sled runners straddles it, its lime cutting arm slicing the last bound bundle of forms from the roof and lowering it into a graphite bin, leaving a single sheet tucked under the wiper. Twin tyre tracks already lead from the cleared car toward the horizon.

title: Can't drop below pace
hero: deadline speedometer gauge
start: A round deadline gauge the size of a saucer stands upright on a graphite stand at the centre of a pale neutral tabletop. Its bezel is brushed graphite with fine machining rings, and its front is sandblasted frosted glass: a plain dial with tick marks and a slim graphite needle. A short acid-lime marker bar is fixed on the dial rim at the middle of the arc, a minimum the needle must stay above, and the needle sits just past it. To the left, a small stack of ivory task cards is squared on a graphite tray. To the right, a frosted acrylic mug and a graphite stapler wait in line. Fine dust lines the bezel's grooves, and the card edges are crisp and slightly fibrous.
end: The same gauge, pinned far above its minimum. The graphite needle trembles hard against the far end of the arc, the acid-lime marker bar now well behind it, and the whole stand vibrates, walking itself across the tabletop. The task cards on the left are being flung off the tray in a rapid stream, skimming through the air in a long flat arc. The mug on the right has slid to the table edge and is tipping, a curl of grey coffee lifting out. The stapler has spun around and is caught mid-skid, trailing a fan of loose staples. Scuff marks run from the stand's feet, a haze of fine dust shakes loose from the bezel, and every flying object streams away from the gauge.
apocalypse: A shattered elevated highway snakes across a wide, dry basin toward a low horizon, its graphite deck sections snapped and sagging between frosted-glass pylons. In the foreground, a giant deadline gauge lies front up on the broken road, its frosted dial cracked and its needle bent against the far end of the arc. Ivory task cards have blown into long drifts along the guard rails and piled in the gaps where the deck fell away. A colossal mug lies shattered in the basin below. In the midground, on an intact span, a slim graphite rail cart has rolled up to the gauge, and its lime brake caliper clamps the bent needle, easing it back toward rest, while a second graphite crane sets new deck plates across the nearest gap.

title: Systems are down
hero: graphite control console with warning lamp
start: A curved control console of brushed graphite metal, about a forearm wide, sits at the front of a pale neutral tabletop. Its angled deck holds rows of small frosted acrylic toggle keys, each softly lit from within, and three blank frosted-glass panels glowing evenly. One small acid-lime warning lamp at the far right blinks, the only fault. Behind the console, a narrow corridor model runs back into the midground, lined with four graphite security doors, all shut, their seams tight. An empty graphite swivel chair is turned toward the deck, with a frosted mug and a crumpled ivory paper sandwich wrapper beside it. Fine dust lies in the gaps between keys, and the doors show faint machining marks.
end: The same console going dark. From the acid-lime warning lamp at the right, the fault spreads leftward: the frosted keys switch off in a rippling line, two of the three panels have gone dull grey and the third flickers. Down the corridor behind, the graphite security doors slide open in sequence, the first fully open, the second halfway, the third just cracked and the fourth still shut, each one tripped by the last. The swivel chair has spun and rolled into the corridor mouth. The mug is tipped, a thin grey spill running into the key gaps. A drift of ivory paper printouts pours from a slot under the console, caught mid-fall, and dust sifts down from the open door frames.
apocalypse: A wide, overgrown ruin spreads toward a misty horizon, thick with fronds and vines cut from ivory paper, curling and yellowed at their tips. The giant graphite console lies tilted in the foreground, its frosted panels cracked and furred with paper moss, keys missing like lost teeth. Beyond it, the corridor has become a long canyon of graphite doors, each as tall as a tower and stuck at a different gap, with paper vines pouring through them. Drifts of old printouts lie matted into the ground. In the midground, a slim graphite cable-laying rig on thin jointed legs threads a line across the canyon floor and pushes a single lime master switch into the console's base, and the first row of frosted keys nearest it glows again.

title: Sinking launch
hero: graphite product-launch barge
start: A tabletop sea of frosted acrylic waves, rippled and softly glowing from within, fills a shallow graphite tray about a forearm long. Riding at its centre is a flat product-launch barge the size of a shoebox, its hull brushed graphite metal with a chamfered bow and neat rivet rows. On its deck sits a single product crate of ivory card, crisply folded and tied with graphite wire. Along the barge's rail hang four small ivory paper lifeboats on graphite davits, and one acid-lime lifebuoy is clipped at the stern. A folded ivory launch plan rests on the tray rim at left, weighted by a graphite paperweight. Fine scuffs mark the hull, and dust sits in the wave grooves.
end: The same barge listing hard to the right. Its bow has dipped under the frosted acrylic waves, and the ivory product crate slides down the tilted deck, its wire snapped and one corner already in the water. Three of the four paper lifeboats have been cut loose from the budget and hang mid-fall from their davits, graphite lines coiling after them; the fourth dangles by one end. The acid-lime lifebuoy has jumped its clip and is caught in the air over the stern. Frosted spray lifts where the bow meets the waves. On the left, the launch plan has been swept off the tray rim and flutters open. Crumpled paper scraps drift on the surface, spreading outward from the hull.
apocalypse: A deep miniature sea floor of pale sediment stretches into dim, milky distance, lit from above through a ceiling of frosted acrylic waves. In the foreground lies the giant barge, broken in two across its middle, its graphite hull crusted with pale paper silt and its davits bent. The product crate has burst open on the seabed, its ivory card walls softened and collapsed. Three paper lifeboats lie scattered across the floor like pale husks. In the midground, a slim graphite salvage rig hangs from a vertical cable that rises out of frame, and its lime grab claw closes around one intact product carton, lifting it upward in a thin plume of silt toward a small graphite pontoon floating dark on the surface above.

title: Booby-trapped office
hero: tripwire across an office doorway
start: A small office corner sits on a pale neutral tabletop: a graphite doorframe about as tall as a coffee mug at left, a graphite desk in the midground and a tall graphite shelf at right. Across the foot of the doorway runs a single taut acid-lime tripwire, fixed to two tiny graphite eyelets. The wire's far end leads along the floor to a graphite stapler perched at the desk's edge. On the desk, a frosted acrylic pencil pot, a row of ivory binders and a roll of ivory tape sit in line, and a rolling graphite chair is parked nearby. The shelf holds a frosted glass jar of marbles and three stacked ivory boxes. Dust gathers along the skirting, and the binder spines show fine creases.
end: The same office mid-cascade, starting at the doorway. The acid-lime tripwire has been snagged and pulled tight, yanking the stapler off the desk edge; it hangs mid-drop and has knocked the pencil pot, which sprays pencils across the desktop. The pencils have struck the rolling chair, which is rolling right into the shelf. The shelf is tipping: the frosted marble jar has tumbled and is emptying, marbles bouncing across the floor, and the ivory boxes slide off in a stepped fall. Binders fan open as they topple like dominoes along the desk. The tape roll unspools across the floor. Dust rises in a line that follows the whole path back to the wire.
apocalypse: A long, narrow ravine winds through a wide ruin toward a pale horizon, its floor littered with oversized office traps long since sprung. Giant graphite shelves lie across it like fallen bridges, and frosted marbles the size of boulders sit where they rolled, filmed with dust. Toppled binders form a crooked ridge along one wall, their ivory covers split and bleached. A snapped graphite doorframe stands at the ravine's mouth, and old wires cross the floor at odd heights. In the midground, a slim six-legged graphite survey walker steps carefully along the ravine, planting small lime stakes on either side to mark one clear, safe path, while a flat graphite roller behind it presses the marked lane smooth and level.

title: Square filter, round hole
hero: square filter cartridge and round intake socket
start: A brushed graphite ventilation console about the size of a toaster sits at the centre of a pale neutral tabletop. On its top panel is a single round intake socket, machined clean with a chamfered lip and four small hex fasteners. Beside it, to the right, rests a square filter cartridge of frosted acrylic, its pleated ivory paper media visible through the milky walls. An acid-lime seal ring runs around its square frame, plainly the wrong shape for the round socket. To the left, a short stack of ivory manuals lies closed beside a roll of ivory tape and a graphite hose clip. Fine dust edges the socket lip, and the paper pleats show soft fibre fuzz.
end: The same console buried in improvised fixes. The square cartridge has been jammed into the round socket at an angle, its acid-lime seal ring buckled and bulging out of the gaps. Ivory tape wraps the join in thick crooked layers, loose tails flying. Stiff manual covers have been torn off and bent into a rough collar, and a ribbed frosted acrylic hose snakes from one gap, clamped with three graphite clips before it kinks and splits; a second hose has been added to the split, then a third. The manuals on the left lie open and gutted, pages drifting off. A puff of pale dust blows out from the leaking seam, frozen in the air, pointing straight back to the socket.
apocalypse: A wide crater of pale ivory dust and bleached tape curls stretches toward a low, hazy horizon. At its centre rises the giant graphite console, cracked and tilted, its round socket choked with an enormous square cartridge wrapped in layers of fossilised tape. Ribbed frosted hoses the size of pipelines coil across the crater floor, split and sagging, and torn manual covers stand upright in the dust like broken fins. In the middle distance, a slim graphite machining rig on a turntable base has milled a lime adapter ring, square on one front and round on the other, and a thin graphite arm lowers it toward the socket, lining its square front up with the old cartridge's frame.

title: Shifting cube rooms
hero: frosted acrylic meeting pod on a sliding grid
start: On a pale neutral tabletop stands a single meeting pod, a cube of frosted acrylic about the size of a tissue box, its edges banded in brushed graphite with small hex fasteners at each corner. One graphite door panel sits closed on its front. Inside, blurred by the milky walls, are a small graphite table and a folded ivory agenda card. The pod rests on a graphite floor grid of square tiles, with one empty square to its right. A single acid-lime door handle on the front panel is the only way out. To the left, a folded ivory jacket hangs on a graphite hook stand, and a frosted mug waits beside the pod. Fine dust lines the grid grooves, and the acrylic shows faint polish swirls.
end: The same pod, now one of many. Identical frosted cubes have filled the graphite grid in rows, sliding and turning on their tiles like a sliding puzzle; three are caught mid-slide with scrape marks behind them, and one is tipped on its side mid-rotation. The original pod has been shunted to the midground, its acid-lime door handle now facing the blank frosted wall of the next cube. Doors on other pods swing open onto more pods. Inside, the agenda card has slipped flat against the glass. A sliding cube has knocked over the hook stand, the jacket half off, and the mug is tipping at the grid edge. Grit sprays from the tile grooves, spreading outward from the original pod's square.
apocalypse: A vast stepped mesa of stacked frosted cubes rises from a pale plain, weathered milky and cracked, staggered and jammed at odd angles, reaching toward a low, hazy horizon. Graphite edge bands have bent and loosened, and dust has settled into the gaps between cubes like mortar. Many doors hang open onto other cubes. In the lower tier, a toppled hook stand juts out, bleached. In the foreground, a slim graphite tracked crane with a long jointed boom has reached into the stack and drawn one cube to the outer front; its lime clamp holds that cube's door open, and a narrow graphite ramp leads from the doorway down to the plain, the first way out to open ground.

title: Contract takes your name
hero: frosted acrylic nameplate beside a contract
start: A clean desk of brushed graphite metal sits on a pale neutral tabletop. At its centre lies a single employment contract of heavy ivory paper with deckled edges and blank ruled lines, a graphite fountain pen resting across it with its cap off. To the right stands a small nameplate block of frosted acrylic, about the size of a chocolate bar, with a smooth acid-lime inlay stripe along its front where a name would be, blank and glowing softly. To the left, a graphite in-tray holds two more folded sheets. A frosted mug of cooling tea has left a faint ring. The paper's fibres catch the light, the pen nib holds a tiny bead of grey ink, and dust rests in the tray's corners.
end: The same desk under rising contracts. Ivory contract sheets pour from the in-tray on the left and climb in slanting stacks across the desk, the tallest leaning over the nameplate. The acid-lime inlay stripe on the nameplate is fading, its glow thinning to a pale wash as sheets slide against it and paper dust settles in its groove. The fountain pen has rolled off and is caught mid-fall past the desk edge, trailing a thin spatter of grey ink. The mug has been nudged to the rim and tips, a curl of tea lifting out. Loose sheets hang in the air above the stacks, and the whole pile leans away from the in-tray, which is still spilling.
apocalypse: A wide, misty marsh of softened ivory paper stretches toward a faint horizon, its surface pooled with still water and dotted with sagging mounds of contracts, their deckled edges curled and grey. In the foreground, a giant graphite desk lies half sunk, and the fountain pen, big as a mast, leans out of the mud. Fog drifts between the stacks. In the midground, the frosted nameplate block stands cracked on a low mound, its front dull. A slim graphite dredging rig on thin stilt legs has cleared the sheets around it and presses a lime polishing wheel against its front, and under the wheel the inlay stripe is glowing clearly again.

title: Denied claims cubicle
hero: graphite rubber stamp in a card cubicle
start: A cramped cubicle made of three ivory card partition walls, each about as tall as a coffee mug with crisp folded edges and graphite trim, stands on a pale neutral tabletop. Inside, a small graphite desk fills most of the floor. On it lies a single ivory claim form with blank boxes, and beside it a graphite rubber stamp with a chamfered body rests on a frosted acrylic ink pad. The stamp's handle cap is acid-lime, the only colour in the frame. A graphite in-tray at the back holds a thin stack of waiting forms. The chair is pushed in with a cardigan draped over it, and a frosted mug sits by the tray. Card fibres show at the partition corners, and fine dust edges the ink pad.
end: The same cubicle closing in. The graphite stamp is caught mid-strike above a fresh form, its acid-lime handle cap blurred with speed, and every sheet it touches carries the same flat grey block mark. Stamped forms stack in towering, slanting piles on the desk and spill from the in-tray in a torrent. The three ivory card partitions bow inward under the pressure, creases buckling, the right wall already folding over the chair. The cardigan has slipped to the floor under a drift of paper. The mug is squeezed against the tray and cracking. Loose forms fly up over the cubicle walls, and grey ink spatter and paper dust hang in the air above the desk.
apocalypse: A narrow canyon of collapsed ivory card walls runs toward a pale horizon, the partitions folded flat and pressed into strata like layered rock by the weight of stamped forms wedged into every crevice. On the canyon floor, a giant graphite stamp lies on its side with its body cracked, and the ink pad beside it has dried into a split grey crust. The desk is crushed flat beneath a slab of forms, only one corner showing. In the midground, a slim graphite sorting rig on a short conveyor lifts forms one at a time from a drift, and its lime stamping arm presses a single clean mark onto one unmarked form, which slides into a neat graphite out-tray standing clear of the rubble.

title: Task board stampede
hero: ivory card task board with frosted tiles
start: A flat game board of ivory card, about the size of a place mat, lies on a pale neutral tabletop, its surface ruled with a winding path of blank squares. Small task tiles of frosted acrylic, each the size of a sugar cube, sit stacked in a neat graphite tray at the board's left end. On the start square rests a single acid-lime token. Two blank-faced graphite dice sit in a frosted glass cup at the front right, waiting. Behind the board, a graphite desk holds a closed laptop and a pen holder, and a jacket hangs over its chair. Card fibres show along the board's folded hinge, and dust sits in the tray's corners.
end: The same board, erupting. The two graphite dice are caught mid-tumble across the board, and from the tray on the left a stampede of frosted task tiles pours out in a dense running wave, hundreds of them hopping and skidding along the path. The acid-lime token has been knocked off its start square and flung into the air. The wave has reached the desk behind: the pen holder is toppled with pens scattering, the laptop is shunted to the edge and tipping, and the chair is driven backward, its jacket flying. Tiles ricochet off the desk legs and skid off the table edge. Card dust and acrylic chips hang in the air, every trail pointing back to the tray.
apocalypse: A trampled plain stretches toward a hazy horizon, its ground churned into ruts and furrows packed with countless worn frosted tiles, chipped and milky, heaped into long ridges where the stampede passed. In the foreground, the giant ivory game board lies torn and curled up like a broken terrace, its path squares faded. The desk is flattened beneath a ridge of tiles, its laptop split open and bleached. A graphite die the size of a building sits embedded in a furrow. In the midground, a slim graphite sorting rig on long spider legs straddles the board, picking tiles from the ruts with a fine clamp and stacking them back in their tray, and its lime pointer arm sets one token squarely back on the start square.

title: Thawed and outdated
inspired_by: Austin Powers: International Man of Mystery (1997)
hero: frosted-glass cryo chamber holding an old computer
start: A tall cryo chamber the size of a wine bottle stands upright at the left of a pale neutral tabletop: a frosted-glass cylinder with a brushed graphite base and cap, its milky walls glowing faintly and misted with frost crystals. Sealed inside, blurred, is a small office desk kit: a boxy old computer with a chunky ivory case and a curved frosted screen, a coiled ivory cord and a graphite keyboard. A single acid-lime thaw lever on the cap is locked upright. To the right stands a current slim graphite dock with a thin port row, a small graphite tray of frosted adapters and a frosted mug. Frost grains dust the base, and a faint mist curls from the seams.
end: The same chamber, thawed and split open. The acid-lime thaw lever has snapped down, and the frosted glass has cracked away in curved shards that hang mid-fall, trailing a sheet of meltwater that fans across the tabletop toward the right. The old computer has slid out on a skid of wet frost, its thick ivory cord uncoiling toward the slim dock, where its chunky plug is jammed crooked against the thin port row, clearly the wrong size. The adapter tray has tipped, scattering mismatched frosted adapters, none of which fit. The mug drifts off in the puddle, tipping. Mist and droplets hang in the air above the chamber base, all spreading from the cracked glass.
apocalypse: A wide glacier of frosted acrylic ice stretches to a white horizon, cracked into slabs and ridges and frozen around the relics of an older office. In the foreground, a giant boxy computer lies half entombed, its ivory case yellowed and split, its curved frosted screen crazed with cracks. Its enormous cord runs across the ice like a frozen river, ending at a toppled graphite dock whose port row is far too thin for it. Broken chamber shards stand upright like icebergs, and hundreds of discarded adapters are sealed into the surface. In the midground, a slim graphite tripod rig with a heated drill has melted a channel between the two, and its lime bridging adapter now sits snug, joining the old plug to the new dock.

title: Overqualified at the counter
hero: record-shop counter with turntable and list cards
start: A record-shop counter of brushed graphite metal, about a forearm long, sits across the midground of a pale neutral tabletop. At its left end stands a small turntable with a frosted acrylic platter and a graphite tonearm resting in its cradle, its acid-lime needle cartridge poised but idle. At the right end lies a neat stack of ivory list cards, each blank and slightly curled, squared against a graphite card box. Behind the counter, a low graphite bin holds a row of plain ivory record sleeves standing upright. In front, three frosted-glass shopping baskets wait in a short line, empty. A cold mug sits by the stack. Card edges show fine fibres, and dust rests on the platter.
end: The same counter, backed up. The ivory list cards have multiplied into a leaning tower on the right that is toppling toward the camera, cards peeling off its top and fanning into the air. The card box has tipped and spilled more across the counter. In front, the line of frosted-glass baskets has grown into a long queue snaking off the left edge, the front baskets heaped with sleeves pulled from the bin and still waiting. The turntable spins untended, its acid-lime needle cartridge jolted up off the platter and the tonearm bouncing. Stray cards have landed on the platter and ride around on it. Paper dust drifts from the toppling stack toward the queue.
apocalypse: A wide plateau of layered ivory list cards, weathered into flaking terraces, stretches toward a low horizon. In the foreground, the giant graphite counter lies cracked across its middle, half sunk in card drifts. A long line of frosted-glass baskets, each the size of a car, runs off into the distance, tilted and filled with bleached sleeves and fallen cards. The record bin has spilled plain sleeves across the ground like fallen slabs. In the midground, the turntable has been dug out: its frosted platter, cracked and dusty, sits level again, and a slim graphite crane arm on a pivoting base lowers a lime needle cartridge gently onto one clean record on the platter, the first groove catching the light.

title: System erased you
hero: ivory employee file folder and access badge
start: A graphite filing cabinet, about the height of a shoebox on end, stands at the right of a pale neutral tabletop, its top drawer pulled open to show a row of ivory folders with unmarked tabs. On the desk in front of it lies a single thick employee file, an ivory folder with crisp creases, holding a blank photo card and ruled sheets. Beside it rests a graphite ID badge on a coiled frosted acrylic lanyard, its acid-lime access strip glowing softly. To the left, a small graphite doorframe stands closed with a frosted-glass badge reader beside it. A mug with a faint coffee ring sits by the file. Fine dust rests in the drawer rails, and fibres show at the folder's edges.
end: The same desk, being cleared. The employee file is emptying itself: sheets lift out one by one and break into drifting flakes of ivory paper dust as they rise, and the photo card has faded to plain white. In the cabinet, the file's slot is closing, pushing the other folders together. The badge's acid-lime access strip has gone dark grey, and the badge lies rejected at the foot of the reader, the door still shut. A flat graphite sweeper arm slides across the desk from the left, having wiped that half bare, and is pushing the mug off the edge, the lanyard sliding after it. Paper dust hangs in a column above the empty folder.
apocalypse: A cavernous vault stretches back into dim depth, walled with towering graphite filing cabinets, some toppled into ramps, others standing with drawers hanging open and emptied. The floor is a deep, pale sediment of ivory paper dust, heaped in drifts against the cabinets. In the foreground, a giant doorframe stands shut, its frosted reader cracked, a bleached badge half buried at its foot. A colossal empty folder lies splayed open like a collapsed tent. In the midground, a slim graphite archive rig runs along overhead rails, its lime folder clamp holding one rebuilt ivory file with its sheets restacked, lowering it into the reopened slot of a single cleaned drawer.

title: Daily sample check
hero: graphite entry turnstile with frosted sample reader
start: A sleek entry turnstile about the height of a coffee pot stands on a pale neutral tabletop, its pillar of brushed graphite metal with chamfered edges and a single frosted-glass gate arm. On top of the pillar sits one compact sample reader, a smooth frosted acrylic block with a small recessed slot. Beside the slot, one acid-lime status light waits, lit steady. In front of the turnstile, three graphite ID badges lie in a neat line on a frosted tray, and a folded ivory visitor pass rests beside them. Behind, a pale lobby floor stretches away, empty and clean. A forgotten graphite umbrella leans on the pillar. Fine polish swirls show on the gate arm, and a trace of dust lines the slot.
end: The same turnstile, grown stricter. A second, then a third frosted reader has been bolted onto the pillar with bulky graphite brackets, each stacked higher and leaning, fasteners bristling. The acid-lime status light on the original reader now blinks, and the frosted gate arm is locked shut. In front, the neat line of badges has become a long queue of badges on frosted trays, snaking back across the lobby floor in tight loops, the rearmost trays sliding into each other. A fourth bracket is caught mid-fall, dropping loose bolts. The visitor pass has blown off and flutters in the air, and the umbrella slides down the pillar. Fine grit from fresh drill holes drifts down.
apocalypse: A vast, pale, perfectly flat lobby floor stretches to a clean horizon under even light, almost spotless but long abandoned. At its centre stands the giant turnstile, now a tower of frosted readers bolted one above another, leaning and cracked, its brackets furred with pale dust. The gate arm is fused shut. Around it, the queue of badge trays forms long curving drifts that coil across the floor into the distance, the trays bleached and chipped. Loose bolts lie scattered like gravel. Beside the tower, a slim graphite rail track has been laid, and a low graphite rig on it has just slid a lime gate panel aside, opening one clean passage alongside the readers, its track running straight past them.

title: Midnight reorg
hero: graphite office floor under tall night windows
start: A model office floor about the size of a tray sits on a pale neutral tabletop, its graphite floor plate scored in a fine grid. Four small graphite desks stand in neat rows, each with a frosted acrylic lamp, an ivory paper notepad and a pushed-in chair. Along the back runs a row of tall sandblasted frosted-glass windows showing dark night blue beyond. Two low ivory card partition walls divide the floor. On the nearest desk, a single acid-lime sticky flag marks a folder left ready for the morning. A graphite coat stand at the left holds one forgotten scarf. The lamps are off, dust lies in the grid grooves, and the notepads show faint indent lines.
end: The same floor mid-rearrangement in the dark. The graphite floor plate has split along its grid into square sections that slide and rotate, one tilted up on an edge, another turning a quarter, each dragging its desk along. The ivory card partitions glide across the floor at odd angles, one caught mid-slide into a desk's path. Chairs roll loose between sections, notepads lift off the desks, and the coat stand topples, its scarf airborne. The desk carrying the acid-lime sticky flag has been swept to the far right corner, its folder sliding off. The frosted windows at the back are shifting sideways too. Grit sprays from the separating seams, every movement circling a common centre.
apocalypse: A wide, tangled ruin spreads under a dark sky, built from office floors the size of city blocks, tilted at clashing angles and stacked into jagged terraces that fade toward a dim horizon. Graphite floor plates overlap like broken slabs, desks cling to slopes or hang from edges, and ivory partitions lie jammed between levels. Frosted windows stand in scattered rows, some upright and some front down. In the midground, one level plate has been cleared, and a slim graphite survey rig on thin tripod legs stakes a lime floor-plan line in a crisp rectangle across it, while a graphite gantry sets the first partition wall along that line and bolts its base plate down.

title: Daily re-onboarding
hero: onboarding cassette on a welcome packet
start: A fresh graphite desk sits on a pale neutral tabletop, bare except for a neat onboarding kit: an ivory card welcome packet, thick and crisply folded with a blank cover, and a small cassette with a frosted acrylic shell and graphite spools resting on top. A compact graphite tape player sits to the right, its lid open. A clean frosted acrylic mug stands on the left, beside a coiled graphite lanyard with a blank badge. The chair is tucked in. On the cassette, a blank acid-lime label strip marks the single note the tape is able to keep. Faint dust lies only at the desk's edges, and the packet's fibres catch the light.
end: The same desk, morning after morning. Welcome packets have piled into tall slumping stacks, each identical and bent open only at its first page, the rest pressed shut and unread. The stacks lean into each other, and one is sliding off the left edge, packets fanning into the air. The tape player's lid has clapped shut on the cassette, and a long loop of shiny tape ribbon spills from it, unwinding across the desk and draping over the packets. The acid-lime label strip is buried under the newest packet. The first mug is now surrounded by a row of identical clean mugs, one set out for each new first day. Paper dust drifts from the sliding stack.
apocalypse: A long, grey shoreline stretches to a pale sea horizon, its tidal flats covered in unspooled tape ribbon lying in coiling lines like washed-up kelp. Mounds of welcome packets have weathered into sodden, layered dunes, their covers bleached and frayed. In the foreground, a giant graphite tape player sits half buried in wet ivory paper sand, its lid cracked and its edges scoured. A row of identical mugs lies tipped along the tideline like stones. In the midground, a slim graphite spooling rig on two wide wheels crawls along the flats, winding the stray tape onto a clean reel, and its lime ejector tray slides one small cassette free from the player, a single saved note card clipped on top.

title: Photo-note handoff
hero: instant-photo notes with a graphite camera
start: A clean graphite desk sits on a pale neutral tabletop, with a small graphite instant camera about the size of a fist at the right, its frosted lens housing catching the light. Across the desk runs a loose, orderly row of four instant-photo notes, each a square of ivory card with a softly blurred frosted image area and a blank caption strip beneath. A single acid-lime pushpin holds a fifth photo to a small ivory corkboard leaning against the back. A capped graphite pen lies across the row. On the left, a folded shift jacket hangs from a hook, and a half-finished mug sits nearby. The card edges curl slightly, and fine dust sits in the camera's grooves.
end: The same desk, buried in photos after a missed handoff. The camera keeps ejecting new prints, one caught mid-slide from its slot, and instant photos have multiplied across the desk, up the corkboard and onto the back wall in overlapping layers, pinned crooked over one another, their blurred images disagreeing. The acid-lime pushpin still holds the first photo, now covered by three others. The pen has rolled off and hangs mid-drop. The jacket has slumped from its hook onto a drift of prints on the floor. The mug has been nudged to the edge and tilts. Prints flip through the air, all fanning out from the camera slot, and paper dust drifts across the layers.
apocalypse: A wide, dusty courtyard ruin opens under a pale sky, ringed by a low row of cracked graphite walls and doorways in a long single storey that fades into haze. Across the ground, thousands of faded instant photos drift in shallow banks, their card edges curled and bleached, their images washed to milky blanks. The giant camera lies on its side at the centre, its lens housing cracked and packed with dust. In the midground, a slim graphite sorting rig on a narrow rail picks prints from the drift one by one and pins them to a short line of low graphite stakes, and a thin lime thread spooled from its arm links the stakes in one clear order toward the nearest wall.

title: Seven-day countdown
hero: seven-segment countdown dial beside a sealed folder
start: A round countdown dial about the size of a saucer stands on a brushed graphite base at the left of a pale neutral tabletop. Its front is sandblasted frosted glass divided into seven wedge segments around a plain centre, all softly lit from within. To the right lies a single project folder of heavy ivory card, closed, with a crisp spine and an unmarked tab, and an acid-lime elastic band stretched once around it, still sealed. Behind, a graphite in-tray holds two loose task cards. A graphite pen rests parallel to the folder, and a frosted mug waits nearby, full. Fine dust edges the dial's segment lines, and the folder's card shows long parallel fibres.
end: The same dial, running down. Four of the seven frosted segments have gone dark grey, a fifth is dimming, and the last two glow faintly. The project folder still lies closed, its acid-lime elastic band untouched, but work has piled up around it: task cards have spilled from the in-tray and banked against the folder in slanting drifts, some caught sliding over its top. The pen has vanished under cards. The mug sits cold with a skin on its surface and has been shoved to the edge by the advancing drift. Loose cards flutter off the right side. A thin dust hangs in front of the dimming segments, and the drift slopes back toward the tray.
apocalypse: A deep, terraced quarry drops away below the viewer, its stepped walls built from thousands of compressed ivory folders, spines bleached, curled and split, descending in broad benches toward a shadowed floor. Beyond the far rim, a pale plain runs to a hazy horizon. On the near rim, the giant countdown dial lies cracked and fully dark, half sunk in a drift of task cards. On the quarry floor, the original project folder sits closed, pinned under loose cards. A slim graphite derrick braced on the rim lowers a lime lifting line straight down, its graphite hook clasped around the folder's spine, and the folder is just beginning to rise, shedding a trickle of cards.

title: Office chain reaction
hero: graphite desk fan aimed at a paper stack
start: A small desk fan with a brushed graphite cage and frosted acrylic blades, about the height of a mug, sits at the left of a pale neutral tabletop, aimed to the right. In front of it lies a loose stack of ivory paper, edges slightly misaligned. Next to the stack stands a full frosted mug, then a graphite power strip whose cord runs back to the fan. Beyond, a slim graphite wall shelf holding three ivory binders is mounted above a second desk in the right background. The fan's acid-lime power switch is just being clicked on, the only colour in the scene. The top sheet's corner curls up, and fine dust sits on the fan cage.
end: The same objects falling in sequence from left to right. The fan spins, its acid-lime switch on, and the top ivory sheet has lifted and flown into the frosted mug, tipping it. A sheet of grey coffee arcs out onto the graphite power strip, which gives a small pale spark and jerks its cord, yanking the shelf bracket loose. The shelf is caught mid-drop, its three ivory binders tumbling open, the first striking the second desk, which tips onto its side. Loose paper swirls in the fan's draught, droplets hang in the air, and dust and scraps trace a clear line from the last falling desk back to the fan.
apocalypse: A long valley stretches toward a hazy horizon, crossed by a line of giant toppled desks and shelves lying one against the next like fallen dominoes, each the size of a building, weathered, cracked and furred with pale dust. Drifts of ivory paper fill the gaps between them. At the near end, the enormous fan lies on its back, its frosted blades cracked. A colossal mug rests on its side, stained grey inside. The chain runs on down the valley, but in the midground the last desk still stands, leaning only slightly, held by a lime stop block that a slim graphite rail tractor has just pushed into place at its base, bracing it against the fall.
